# Skeema

Skeema is a tool for managing MySQL and MariaDB schema changes in a declarative fashion using pure SQL. The Skeema CLI tool allows you to:

* Export `CREATE TABLE` statements to the filesystem, for tracking in a Git repo
* Diff changes in the schema repo against live DBs to automatically generate DDL
* Manage multiple environments (e.g. dev, staging, prod) and keep them in sync with ease
* Configure use of online schema change tools, such as `pt-online-schema-change`, `gh-ost`, or `spirit`, for performing `ALTER TABLE`
* Apply configurable linter rules to proactively catch schema design problems and enforce company policies

Skeema supports a pull-request-based workflow for schema change submission, review, and execution. This permits your team to manage schema changes in exactly the same way as you manage code changes.

## Products and Downloads

This repo is the free open source Community edition of the Skeema command-line tool. The Community edition supports management of **tables** and **routines** (procs/funcs). Builds are provided for Linux and MacOS.

The paid Premium edition of the Skeema CLI adds support for managing **views**, **triggers**, and **events**. It also includes a native **Windows build**, built-in **SSH tunnel** functionality, **seed data** management, and many other improvements.

For download links and more information, visit [skeema.io](https://www.skeema.io/download/).

Usage:  skeema lint [<options>] [<environment>]

Checks for problems in filesystem representation of database objects. A set of
linter rules are run against all objects. Each rule may be configured to
generate an error, a warning, or be ignored entirely. Statements that contain
invalid SQL, or otherwise return an error from the database, are always flagged
as linter errors.

By default, this command also reformats CREATE statements to their canonical
form, just like `skeema format`.

This command relies on accessing a database server to test the SQL DDL in a
temporary location. See the --workspace option for more information.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for linter configuration
and workspace selection. For example, running `skeema lint staging` will apply
config directives from the [staging] section of config files, as well as any
sectionless directives at the top of the file. If no environment name is
supplied, the default is "production".

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no errors or warnings were emitted and all
files were already formatted properly; 1 if any warnings were emitted and/or
some files were reformatted; or 2+ if any errors were emitted for any reason.

      --strip-partitioning         Remove PARTITION BY clauses from *.sql files

      --allow-compression value    List of allowed compression settings for --lint-compression (default "none,4kb,8kb")

Usage:  skeema init [<options>] [<environment>]

Creates a filesystem representation of the schemas on a database server. For
each schema on the DB server (or just the single schema specified by --schema),
a subdir with a .skeema config file will be created. Each directory will be
populated with .sql files containing CREATE statements for every table and
routine in the schema.

When operating on all schemas on the server, this command automatically skips
pre-installed / system schemas (information_schema, performance_schema, mysql,
sys, test).

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files the host-related options are
written to. For example, running `skeema init staging` will add config
directives to the [staging] section of config files. If no environment name is
supplied, the default is "production", so directives will be written to the
[production] section of the file.

Init Options:
  -d, --dir value              Subdir name to use for this host's schemas (default "<hostname>")
  -h, --host value             Database hostname or IP address
      --include-auto-inc       Include starting auto-inc values in table files
  -P, --port value             Port to use for database host (default "3306")
      --schema value           Only import the one specified schema; skip creation of subdirs for each schema

Usage:  skeema format [<options>] [<environment>]

Reformats the filesystem representation of database objects to match the
canonical format shown in SHOW CREATE.

This command relies on accessing a database server to test the SQL DDL in a
temporary location. See the --workspace option for more information.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for workspace selection.
For example, running `skeema format staging` will apply config directives from
the [staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at
the top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

An exit code of 0 will be returned if all files were already formatted properly;
1 if some files were not already in the correct format; or 2+ if any errors
occurred.

Format Options:

      --[skip-]write               Update files to correct format (enabled by default; disable with --skip-write)

Workspace Options:

===== /tmp/skeema_help/help_add-environment.txt =====
Modifies the .skeema file in an existing host directory to add a new named
environment. For example, if `skeema init` was previously used to create a dir
for a host with the default "production" environment, `skeema add-environment`
could be used to define a "staging" or "development" environment pointing at a
different host and port, or perhaps a "local" environment pointing at localhost
and a socket path.

This command currently only handles very simple cases. For many situations,
editing .skeema files directly is a better approach.

===== /tmp/skeema_help/help_init.txt =====
Creates a filesystem representation of the schemas on a database server. For
each schema on the DB server (or just the single schema specified by --schema),
a subdir with a .skeema config file will be created. Each directory will be
populated with .sql files containing CREATE statements for every table and
routine in the schema.

When operating on all schemas on the server, this command automatically skips
pre-installed / system schemas (information_schema, performance_schema, mysql,
sys, test).

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files the host-related options are
written to. For example, running `skeema init staging` will add config
directives to the [staging] section of config files. If no environment name is
supplied, the default is "production", so directives will be written to the
[production] section of the file.

===== /tmp/skeema_help/help_format.txt =====
Reformats the filesystem representation of database objects to match the
canonical format shown in SHOW CREATE.

This command relies on accessing a database server to test the SQL DDL in a
temporary location. See the --workspace option for more information.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for workspace selection.
For example, running `skeema format staging` will apply config directives from
the [staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at
the top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

An exit code of 0 will be returned if all files were already formatted properly;
1 if some files were not already in the correct format; or 2+ if any errors
occurred.

===== /tmp/skeema_help/help_pull.txt =====
Updates the existing filesystem representation of the schemas on a DB server.
Use this command when changes have been applied to the database manually or
outside of Skeema, in order to make the filesystem representation reflect those
changes.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running `skeema pull staging` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

===== /tmp/skeema_help/help_lint.txt =====
Checks for problems in filesystem representation of database objects. A set of
linter rules are run against all objects. Each rule may be configured to
generate an error, a warning, or be ignored entirely. Statements that contain
invalid SQL, or otherwise return an error from the database, are always flagged
as linter errors.

By default, this command also reformats CREATE statements to their canonical
form, just like `skeema format`.

This command relies on accessing a database server to test the SQL DDL in a
temporary location. See the --workspace option for more information.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for linter configuration
and workspace selection. For example, running `skeema lint staging` will apply
config directives from the [staging] section of config files, as well as any
sectionless directives at the top of the file. If no environment name is
supplied, the default is "production".

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no errors or warnings were emitted and all
files were already formatted properly; 1 if any warnings were emitted and/or
some files were reformatted; or 2+ if any errors were emitted for any reason.

===== /tmp/skeema_help/help_diff.txt =====
Compares the schemas on database server(s) to the corresponding filesystem
representation of them. The output is a series of DDL commands that, if run on
the DB server, would cause its schemas to now match the definitions from the
filesystem.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running `skeema diff staging` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

The `skeema diff` command is equivalent to running `skeema push` with its
--dry-run option enabled.

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no differences were found; 1 if some
differences were found; or 2+ if an error occurred.

===== /tmp/skeema_help/help_push.txt =====
Modifies the schemas on database server(s) to match the corresponding filesystem
representation of them. This essentially performs the same diff logic as `skeema
diff`, but then actually runs the generated DDL. You should generally run
`skeema diff` first to see what changes will be applied.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running `skeema push staging` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

An exit code of 0 will be returned if the operation was fully successful; 1 if
at least one table could not be updated due to use of unsupported features, or

error occurred.

var workspaceOptions = OptionGroup{

		{Long: "temp-schema-mode", Type: OptValue, Default: "regular", HasDefault: true, Description: `Tunes workspace load with workspace=temp-schema; heavier load makes Skeema faster but may disrupt other workloads on the database (valid values: "serial", "light", "regular", "heavy", "extreme")`},

		{Short: 'w', Long: "workspace", Type: OptValue, Default: "temp-schema", HasDefault: true, Description: `Specifies where to run intermediate operations (valid values: "temp-schema", "docker")`},

var linterRuleOptions = OptionGroup{

		{Long: "allow-charset", Type: OptValue, Default: "latin1,utf8mb4", HasDefault: true, Description: "List of allowed character sets for --lint-charset"},
		{Long: "allow-compression", Type: OptValue, Default: "none,4kb,8kb", HasDefault: true, Description: "List of allowed compression settings for --lint-compression"},

}

package main

// Define all skeema commands.

var cmdSuite = Command{
	Name:   "skeema",
	Usage:  "[<options>] <command>",
	Suite:  true,
	DocURL: "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands",
	LongDesc: `Skeema is a declarative schema management system for MySQL and MariaDB. It
allows you to export a database schema to the filesystem, and apply online
schema changes by modifying CREATE statements in .sql files.`,
	OptionGroups: []OptionGroup{globalOptions},
}

var cmdAddEnvironment = Command{
	Name:      "add-environment",
	Usage:     "add-environment [<options>] <environment>",
	ShortDesc: "Add a new named environment to an existing host directory",
	DocURL:    "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/add-environment",
	MinArgs:   1,
	MaxArgs:   1,
	LongDesc: `Modifies the .skeema file in an existing host directory to add a new named
environment. For example, if ` + "`skeema init`" + ` was previously used to create a dir
for a host with the default "production" environment, ` + "`skeema add-environment`" + `
could be used to define a "staging" or "development" environment pointing at a
different host and port, or perhaps a "local" environment pointing at localhost
and a socket path.

This command currently only handles very simple cases. For many situations,
editing .skeema files directly is a better approach.`,
	OptionGroups: []OptionGroup{
		{
			Title: "Add-Environment Options:",
			Options: []Option{
				{Short: 'd', Long: "dir", Type: OptValue, Default: ".", HasDefault: true, Description: "Base dir for this host's schemas"},
				{Short: 'h', Long: "host", Type: OptValue, Description: "Database hostname or IP address"},
				{Short: 'P', Long: "port", Type: OptValue, Default: "3306", HasDefault: true, Description: "Port to use for database host"},
				{Short: 'S', Long: "socket", Type: OptValue, Default: "/tmp/mysql.sock", HasDefault: true, Description: "Absolute path to Unix socket file used if host is localhost"},
			},
		},
		globalOptions,
	},
}

var cmdInit = Command{
	Name:      "init",
	Usage:     "init [<options>] [<environment>]",
	ShortDesc: "Save a DB server's schemas to the filesystem",
	DocURL:    "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/init",
	MaxArgs:   1,
	LongDesc: `Creates a filesystem representation of the schemas on a database server. For
each schema on the DB server (or just the single schema specified by --schema),
a subdir with a .skeema config file will be created. Each directory will be
populated with .sql files containing CREATE statements for every table and
routine in the schema.

When operating on all schemas on the server, this command automatically skips
pre-installed / system schemas (information_schema, performance_schema, mysql,
sys, test).

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files the host-related options are
written to. For example, running ` + "`skeema init staging`" + ` will add config
directives to the [staging] section of config files. If no environment name is
supplied, the default is "production", so directives will be written to the
[production] section of the file.`,
	OptionGroups: []OptionGroup{
		{
			Title: "Init Options:",
			Options: []Option{
				{Short: 'd', Long: "dir", Type: OptValue, Default: "<hostname>", HasDefault: true, Description: "Subdir name to use for this host's schemas"},
				{Short: 'h', Long: "host", Type: OptValue, Description: "Database hostname or IP address"},
				{Long: "include-auto-inc", Type: OptBool, Description: "Include starting auto-inc values in table files"},
				{Short: 'P', Long: "port", Type: OptValue, Default: "3306", HasDefault: true, Description: "Port to use for database host"},
				{Long: "schema", Type: OptValue, Description: "Only import the one specified schema; skip creation of subdirs for each schema"},
				{Short: 'S', Long: "socket", Type: OptValue, Default: "/tmp/mysql.sock", HasDefault: true, Description: "Absolute path to Unix socket file used if host is localhost"},
				{Long: "strip-partitioning", Type: OptBool, Description: "Omit PARTITION BY clause when writing partitioned tables to filesystem"},
			},
		},
		globalOptions,
	},
}

var cmdFormat = Command{
	Name:      "format",
	Usage:     "format [<options>] [<environment>]",
	ShortDesc: "Normalize format of filesystem representation of database objects",
	DocURL:    "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/format",
	MaxArgs:   1,
	LongDesc: `Reformats the filesystem representation of database objects to match the
canonical format shown in SHOW CREATE.

This command relies on accessing a database server to test the SQL DDL in a
temporary location. See the --workspace option for more information.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for workspace selection.
For example, running ` + "`skeema format staging`" + ` will apply config directives from
the [staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at
the top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

An exit code of 0 will be returned if all files were already formatted properly;
1 if some files were not already in the correct format; or 2+ if any errors
occurred.`,
	OptionGroups: []OptionGroup{
		{
			Title: "Format Options:",
			Options: []Option{
				{Long: "strip-partitioning", Type: OptBool, Description: "Remove PARTITION BY clauses from *.sql files"},
				{Long: "write", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Update files to correct format (enabled by default; disable with --skip-write)"},
			},
		},
		workspaceOptions,
		globalOptions,
	},
}

var cmdPull = Command{
	Name:      "pull",
	Usage:     "pull [<options>] [<environment>]",
	ShortDesc: "Update the filesystem representation of schemas",
	DocURL:    "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/pull",
	MaxArgs:   1,
	LongDesc: `Updates the existing filesystem representation of the schemas on a DB server.
Use this command when changes have been applied to the database manually or
outside of Skeema, in order to make the filesystem representation reflect those
changes.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running ` + "`skeema pull staging`" + ` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".`,
	OptionGroups: []OptionGroup{
		{
			Title: "Pull Options:",
			Options: []Option{
				{Long: "format", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Reformat SQL statements to match canonical SHOW CREATE (enabled by default; disable with --skip-format)"},
				{Long: "include-auto-inc", Type: OptBool, Description: "Include starting auto-inc values in new table files, and update in existing files"},
				{Long: "new-schemas", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Detect any new schemas and populate new dirs for them (enabled by default; disable with --skip-new-schemas)"},
				{Long: "strip-partitioning", Type: OptBool, Description: "Omit PARTITION BY clause when writing partitioned tables to filesystem"},
				{Long: "update-partitioning", Type: OptBool, Description: "Update PARTITION BY clauses in existing table files"},
			},
		},
		workspaceOptions,
		globalOptions,
	},
}

var cmdLint = Command{
	Name:      "lint",
	Usage:     "lint [<options>] [<environment>]",
	ShortDesc: "Check for problems in filesystem representation of database objects",
	DocURL:    "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/lint",
	MaxArgs:   1,
	LongDesc: `Checks for problems in filesystem representation of database objects. A set of
linter rules are run against all objects. Each rule may be configured to
generate an error, a warning, or be ignored entirely. Statements that contain
invalid SQL, or otherwise return an error from the database, are always flagged
as linter errors.

By default, this command also reformats CREATE statements to their canonical
form, just like ` + "`skeema format`" + `.

This command relies on accessing a database server to test the SQL DDL in a
temporary location. See the --workspace option for more information.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for linter configuration
and workspace selection. For example, running ` + "`skeema lint staging`" + ` will apply
config directives from the [staging] section of config files, as well as any
sectionless directives at the top of the file. If no environment name is
supplied, the default is "production".

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no errors or warnings were emitted and all
files were already formatted properly; 1 if any warnings were emitted and/or
some files were reformatted; or 2+ if any errors were emitted for any reason.`,
	OptionGroups: []OptionGroup{
		{
			Title: "Format Options:",
			Options: []Option{
				{Long: "format", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Reformat SQL statements to match canonical SHOW CREATE (enabled by default; disable with --skip-format)"},
				{Long: "strip-partitioning", Type: OptBool, Description: "Remove PARTITION BY clauses from *.sql files"},
			},
		},
		linterRuleOptions,
		workspaceOptions,
		globalOptions,
	},
}

// sharedDiffPushOptionGroups returns the option groups shared between diff and push,
// differing only in text that varies between the two commands.
func sharedDiffPushOptionGroups(isPush bool) []OptionGroup {
	alterWrapperDesc := "Output ALTER TABLEs as shell commands rather than just raw DDL; see manual for template vars"
	if isPush {
		alterWrapperDesc = "External bin to shell out to for ALTER TABLE; see manual for template vars"
	}
	externalTool := OptionGroup{
		Title: "External Tool Options:",
		Options: []Option{
			{Short: 'x', Long: "alter-wrapper", Type: OptValue, Description: alterWrapperDesc},
			{Long: "alter-wrapper-min-size", Type: OptValue, Default: "0", HasDefault: true, Description: "Ignore --alter-wrapper for tables smaller than this size in bytes"},
			{Short: 'X', Long: "ddl-wrapper", Type: OptValue, Description: "Like --alter-wrapper, but applies to all DDL types (CREATE, DROP, ALTER)"},
		},
	}

	sqlGen := OptionGroup{
		Title: "SQL Generation Options:",
		Options: []Option{
			{Long: "alter-algorithm", Type: OptValue, Description: `Apply an ALGORITHM clause to all ALTER TABLEs (valid values: "inplace", "copy", "instant", "nocopy")`},
			{Long: "alter-lock", Type: OptValue, Description: `Apply a LOCK clause to all ALTER TABLEs (valid values: "none", "shared", "exclusive")`},
			{Long: "alter-validate-virtual", Type: OptBool, Description: "Apply a WITH VALIDATION clause to ALTER TABLEs affecting virtual columns"},
			{Long: "compare-metadata", Type: OptBool, Description: "For stored programs, detect changes to creation-time sql_mode or DB collation"},
			{Long: "exact-match", Type: OptBool, Description: "Follow *.sql table definitions exactly, even for differences with no functional impact"},
			{Long: "lax-column-order", Type: OptBool, Description: "When comparing tables, don't re-order columns if they only differ by position"},
			{Long: "lax-comments", Type: OptBool, Description: "When comparing tables or routines, don't modify them if they only differ by comment clauses"},
			{Long: "partitioning", Type: OptValue, Default: "keep", HasDefault: true, Description: `Specify handling of partitioning status on the database side (valid values: "keep", "remove", "modify")`},
		},
	}

	linter := OptionGroup{Title: "Linter Rule Options:"}
	linter.Options = append(linter.Options, linterRuleOptions.Options[:6]...)
	linter.Options = append(linter.Options, Option{Long: "lint", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Check modified objects for problems before proceeding (enabled by default; disable with --skip-lint)"})
	linter.Options = append(linter.Options, linterRuleOptions.Options[6:]...)

	var safety OptionGroup
	if isPush {
		safety = OptionGroup{
			Title: "Safety Options:",
			Options: []Option{
				{Long: "allow-unsafe", Type: OptBool, Description: "Permit running ALTER or DROP operations that are potentially destructive"},
				{Long: "dry-run", Type: OptBool, Description: "Output DDL but don't run it; equivalent to `skeema diff`"},
				{Long: "foreign-key-checks", Type: OptBool, Description: "Force the server to check referential integrity of any new foreign key"},
				{Long: "safe-below-size", Type: OptValue, Default: "0", HasDefault: true, Description: "Always permit destructive operations for tables below this size in bytes"},
				{Long: "verify", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Test all generated ALTER statements on temp schema to verify correctness (enabled by default; disable with --skip-verify)"},
			},
		}
	} else {
		safety = OptionGroup{
			Title: "Safety Options:",
			Options: []Option{
				{Long: "allow-unsafe", Type: OptBool, Description: "Permit generating ALTER or DROP operations that are potentially destructive"},
				{Long: "safe-below-size", Type: OptValue, Default: "0", HasDefault: true, Description: "Always permit generating destructive operations for tables below this size in bytes"},
				{Long: "verify", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Test all generated ALTER statements on temp schema to verify correctness (enabled by default; disable with --skip-verify)"},
			},
		}
	}

	sharding := OptionGroup{
		Title: "Sharding Options:",
		Options: []Option{
			{Short: 'c', Long: "concurrent-servers", Type: OptValue, Default: "1", HasDefault: true, Description: "Perform operations on this number of database servers concurrently"},
			{Short: '1', Long: "first-only", Type: OptBool, Description: "For dirs mapping to multiple hosts or schemas, only run against the first target per dir"},
		},
	}
	if !isPush {
		sharding.Options = append(sharding.Options, Option{Short: 'q', Long: "brief", Type: OptBool, Description: "Don't output DDL to STDOUT; instead output list of database servers with at least one difference"})
	}

	return []OptionGroup{externalTool, sqlGen, linter, safety, sharding, workspaceOptions, globalOptions}
}

var cmdDiff = Command{
	Name:      "diff",
	Usage:     "diff [<options>] [<environment>]",
	ShortDesc: "Compare a DB server's schemas to the filesystem",
	DocURL:    "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/diff",
	MaxArgs:   1,
	LongDesc: `Compares the schemas on database server(s) to the corresponding filesystem
representation of them. The output is a series of DDL commands that, if run on
the DB server, would cause its schemas to now match the definitions from the
filesystem.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running ` + "`skeema diff staging`" + ` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

The ` + "`skeema diff`" + ` command is equivalent to running ` + "`skeema push`" + ` with its
--dry-run option enabled.

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no differences were found; 1 if some
differences were found; or 2+ if an error occurred.`,
	OptionGroups: sharedDiffPushOptionGroups(false),
}

var cmdPush = Command{
	Name:      "push",
	Usage:     "push [<options>] [<environment>]",
	ShortDesc: "Alter objects on DBs to reflect the filesystem representation",
	DocURL:    "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/push",
	MaxArgs:   1,
	LongDesc: `Modifies the schemas on database server(s) to match the corresponding filesystem
representation of them. This essentially performs the same diff logic as ` + "`skeema" + `
` + "diff`" + `, but then actually runs the generated DDL. You should generally run
` + "`skeema diff`" + ` first to see what changes will be applied.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running ` + "`skeema push staging`" + ` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

An exit code of 0 will be returned if the operation was fully successful; 1 if
at least one table could not be updated due to use of unsupported features, or
if the --dry-run option was used and differences were found; or 2+ if a fatal
error occurred.`,
	OptionGroups: sharedDiffPushOptionGroups(true),
}

var cmdVersion = Command{
	Name:         "version",
	Usage:        "version [<options>]",
	ShortDesc:    "Display program version",
	DocURL:       "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/version",
	LongDesc:     "Display program version",
	OptionGroups: []OptionGroup{globalOptions},
}

var cmdHelp = Command{
	Name:         "help",
	Usage:        "help [<command>]",
	ShortDesc:    "Display usage information",
	Suite:        true, // help shows the main overview
	DocURL:       "https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/help",
	MaxArgs:      1,
	OptionGroups: []OptionGroup{globalOptions},
	LongDesc: `Skeema is a declarative schema management system for MySQL and MariaDB. It
allows you to export a database schema to the filesystem, and apply online
schema changes by modifying CREATE statements in .sql files.`,
}

// Commands is the ordered list of all commands (alphabetical for main help listing).
var allCommands = []*Command{
	&cmdAddEnvironment,
	&cmdDiff,
	&cmdFormat,
	&cmdHelp,
	&cmdInit,
	&cmdLint,
	&cmdPull,
	&cmdPush,
	&cmdVersion,
}

func findCommand(name string) *Command {
	for _, c := range allCommands {
		if c.Name == name {
			return c
		}
	}
	return nil
}
GOEOF

// sharedDiffPushOptionGroups returns the option groups shared between diff and push,
// differing only in text that varies between the two commands.
func sharedDiffPushOptionGroups(isPush bool) []OptionGroup {
	alterWrapperDesc := "Output ALTER TABLEs as shell commands rather than just raw DDL; see manual for template vars"
	if isPush {
		alterWrapperDesc = "External bin to shell out to for ALTER TABLE; see manual for template vars"
	}

			{Short: 'X', Long: "ddl-wrapper", Type: OptValue, Description: "Like --alter-wrapper, but applies to all DDL types (CREATE, DROP, ALTER)"},
		},
	}

	sqlGen := OptionGroup{
		Title: "SQL Generation Options:",
		Options: []Option{
			{Long: "alter-algorithm", Type: OptValue, Description: `Apply an ALGORITHM clause to all ALTER TABLEs (valid values: "inplace", "copy", "instant", "nocopy")`},
			{Long: "alter-lock", Type: OptValue, Description: `Apply a LOCK clause to all ALTER TABLEs (valid values: "none", "shared", "exclusive")`},
			{Long: "alter-validate-virtual", Type: OptBool, Description: "Apply a WITH VALIDATION clause to ALTER TABLEs affecting virtual columns"},
			{Long: "compare-metadata", Type: OptBool, Description: "For stored programs, detect changes to creation-time sql_mode or DB collation"},
			{Long: "exact-match", Type: OptBool, Description: "Follow *.sql table definitions exactly, even for differences with no functional impact"},
			{Long: "lax-column-order", Type: OptBool, Description: "When comparing tables, don't re-order columns if they only differ by position"},
			{Long: "lax-comments", Type: OptBool, Description: "When comparing tables or routines, don't modify them if they only differ by comment clauses"},
			{Long: "partitioning", Type: OptValue, Default: "keep", HasDefault: true, Description: `Specify handling of partitioning status on the database side (valid values: "keep", "remove", "modify")`},
		},
	}

	linter := OptionGroup{Title: "Linter Rule Options:"}
	linter.Options = append(linter.Options, linterRuleOptions.Options[:6]...)
	linter.Options = append(linter.Options, Option{Long: "lint", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Check modified objects for problems before proceeding (enabled by default; disable with --skip-lint)"})
	linter.Options = append(linter.Options, linterRuleOptions.Options[6:]...)

	var safety OptionGroup
	if isPush {

			Title: "Safety Options:",

			},
		}
	} else {
		safety = OptionGroup{
			Title: "Safety Options:",
			Options: []Option{
				{Long: "allow-unsafe", Type: OptBool, Description: "Permit generating ALTER or DROP operations that are potentially destructive"},
				{Long: "safe-below-size", Type: OptValue, Default: "0", HasDefault: true, Description: "Always permit generating destructive operations for tables below this size in bytes"},
				{Long: "verify", Type: OptSkipBool, Description: "Test all generated ALTER statements on temp schema to verify correctness (enabled by default; disable with --skip-verify)"},
			},
		}
	}

	sharding := OptionGroup{
		Title: "Sharding Options:",
		Options: []Option{
			{Short: 'c', Long: "concurrent-servers", Type: OptValue, Default: "1", HasDefault: true, Description: "Perform operations on this number of database servers concurrently"},
			{Short: '1', Long: "first-only", Type: OptBool, Description: "For dirs mapping to multiple hosts or schemas, only run against the first target per dir"},
		},
	}

		sharding.Options = append(sharding.Options, Option{Short: 'q', Long: "brief", Type: OptBool, Description: "Don't output DDL to STDOUT; instead output list of database servers with at least one difference"})
	}

	return []OptionGroup{externalTool, sqlGen, linter, safety, sharding, workspaceOptions, globalOptions}
}

    pass=$((pass+1))

echo "Passed: $pass / $((pass+fail))"

cd /workspace && 
# Run a wider battery of tests
declare -a tests=(
  "" "version" "--version" "help" "--help" "-?"
  "nosuch" "--nosuch" "-x"
  "help diff" "help help" "help version" "help a" "help a b"
  "version help" "version help a"
  "init" "init --host=foo" "init -h foo" "init --debug --host=foo"
  "add-environment" "add-environment myenv" "add-environment --dir=/nonexistent myenv"
  "format" "lint" "diff" "push" "pull"
  "format format" "format help" "lint help"
  "--debug version" "--debug help" "--debug nosuch"
  "--password=foo version" "--password= version" "--password version"
  "--user foo version" "--user --help"
  "-p= version"
  "--skip-my-cnf version" "--my-cnf version"
  "--help=diff" "--help=nosuch" "--help diff"
  "-?diff" "-? diff" "-?nosuch"
  "version extra"
  "help help help help a b c"
)
pass=0
fail=0
for t in "${tests[@]}"; do
  out_new=$(./executable.new $t 2>&1)
  exit_new=$?
  out_old=$(./executable $t 2>&1)
  exit_old=$?
  n_new=$(echo "$out_new" | sed 's/^[0-9-]\{10\} [0-9:]\{8\}/DT/')
  n_old=$(echo "$out_old" | sed 's/^[0-9-]\{10\} [0-9:]\{8\}/DT/')
  if [ "$exit_new" != "$exit_old" ] || [ "$n_new" != "$n_old" ]; then
    fail=$((fail+1))
    echo "FAIL: '$t' (new_exit=$exit_new old_exit=$exit_old)"
    diff <(echo "$n_new") <(echo "$n_old") | head
  else
    pass=$((pass+1))
  fi
done
echo "Passed: $pass / $((pass+fail))"
